Underwater VLC link explorer (v4)

Pick the parts of a link and see the simulated signal-to-noise ratio (300–3000 Hz, at the headphones). Every number here was computed by the v4 simulator's closed-form engine from ngspice analyses of the receiver circuits; nothing is a measurement. The team's requirement is 14 dB.

Build a link

v3 receiver front end (100 kΩ amplifier with the ambient-light servo). Pick the conditions, then change any part and watch the result. The bars underneath show what each alternative for one part would give with the other parts left as they are. Under the hard conditions lamp hum is usually the limit, and the ranking of the parts changes.

The lowest row is what limits this link.

Change one part

Bar = SNR with that option (scale −20 to 55 dB); the thin mark is the 14 dB requirement. Grey = the receiver's front end is overloaded there, so the number is not valid. Click an option to select it. Collimating lenses are modelled as ideal Gaussian beams.

Distance curves

Any of the five receiver presets against distance, in eight waters and four light levels. Scattered light is counted the way a photon-tracing study found it arrives (most of it still reaches the receiver from a wide LED, less from a narrow lens). Pin a curve to compare it with the next selection.

Gaps in a curve are distances where the front end is overloaded. The dashed line is the 14 dB requirement.
